## Unit 10G.3 Fix — Closure Review Rate/Pay Not Showing

**Requirement:** the Manager Closure Review popup was reported as still not showing worker hourly rate/pay (only Total Hours/Sessions/session duration visible) despite Unit 10G.3's formatting pass. Investigate the full data flow (backend query → action DTO → component props → `canViewCosts` rendering) and fix whatever is dropping the data, without touching schema, work-session calculation, `hourly_rate_snapshot` behavior, or exposing costs to Data Entry.

**Investigation (Tasks 1/2):** re-read `getClosureReviewDetailAction` (`app/actions/closure-requests.ts`) end to end and `closure-review-modal.tsx` end to end. Found **no code defect** in either file:
- The action computes `canViewCosts` once via the canonical `canViewCostsForContext` (`lib/security/permissions.ts`) and correctly threads it into `workers[].hourlyRate`, `workers[].totalPay`, `totalAmount`, and the returned `canViewCosts` field itself — all `null` server-side (not merely hidden) whenever the gate is false.
- The component receives `canViewCosts` from `detail.canViewCosts` (the action's own computed value, not re-derived client-side) and passes it down to both `WorkerReviewCard` and `SessionTable`, which gate the Hourly Rate/Total Pay/session Pay lines correctly.

**Root cause:** not a code defect. The seeded "manager" test account(s) (role `maintenance_manager`) have `profiles.can_view_costs = false`, and the `maintenance_manager` role itself is not granted the `costs.view` permission — so `canViewCosts()` legitimately evaluates to `false` for that account, exactly as it would on every other cost-gated screen in the app (Worker Activity, Job Card detail, Daily Activity), since they all use the same canonical helper. Only `super_admin` bypasses via `hasPermission`'s own logic regardless of the profile flag. Confirmed via `scripts/verify-closure-review-payment-display-unit10g3fix.mjs`'s read-only section: both seeded `maintenance_manager` profiles have `can_view_costs=false`, and the role has 0 of its 25 permissions named `costs.view`. This is a seed/permission **data** characteristic (documented in `CLAUDE.md`'s Current Database State baseline), not something this unit changed or should silently change — granting cost visibility to a role/profile is a security-relevant, app-wide decision left to the user.

**Genuine gap found and fixed (Task 3):** `SessionRow.edited_by_name` was already fetched by `getSessionsForAssignmentAction` but never rendered in the Closure Review popup's session rows. Added it next to `correction_reason` in `SessionTable` (`components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx`): `Reason: {reason} · Edited by: {edited_by_name}`. `duration_minutes`/`calculated_amount`/`started_at`/`stopped_at`(`ended_at`)/`status` were already displayed.

**Files changed:** `components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx` (one addition: `edited_by_name` display). `app/actions/closure-requests.ts` unchanged — no bug found there. `scripts/verify-closure-review-payment-display-unit10g3fix.mjs` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration, no schema change, no calculation change, no `hourly_rate_snapshot` behavior change. Data Entry still cannot reach this popup (Manager-only dashboard section) and still receives `null` cost fields wherever `canViewCosts` is checked elsewhere in the app.

**Open item for the user:** if rate/pay should be visible when testing with the seeded "manager" account, either set `profiles.can_view_costs = true` on that profile or grant the `maintenance_manager` role the `costs.view` permission — a data/permission decision, not a code change, and left to the user to authorize since it affects cost visibility app-wide for that account, not just Closure Review. The "System Administrator" super_admin seed account already has `can_view_costs = true` and can be used to see the feature working end to end today.

## Unit 10G.4 — Admin Cost Visibility Toggle for Manager Users

**Requirement:** the Super Admin Users page had no way to grant `can_view_costs` to a user — Unit 10G.3 Fix's finding was that the seeded "manager" test account legitimately has `can_view_costs = false`, and there was no UI to change it short of a direct DB write. Add a Super Admin-only "Cost Access" control on the admin user detail page.

**Server action:** `updateUserCostAccessAction` (new, `app/actions/user-access.ts`) — follows this file's existing `toggleUserActiveAction`/`archiveUserAction` pattern exactly: `requirePermission("admin.users.manage")`, then a hard `context.role?.slug !== "super_admin"` gate (redirect `insufficient-permissions` otherwise), Zod-parsed `profile_id`/`can_view_costs` from a plain `<form action>` (checkbox semantics: unchecked box is simply absent from `FormData`, so the same `z.preprocess((v) => v === "true", z.boolean())` idiom used by `toggleUserActiveAction` correctly resolves absence to `false`), a single `profiles.update({ data: { can_view_costs } })`, `writeAuditLog` with action `user.cost_access_updated` and `{ can_view_costs }` metadata, `emitRealtimeEvent(REALTIME_EVENTS.USER_UPDATED)` (the same event `toggleUserActiveAction` emits — `RealtimeRefresh watch={["user."]}` already active on this page), `revalidatePath`, redirect with `?success=cost-access-updated`. Writes only `profiles.can_view_costs` — never touches `role_permissions`/`costs.view`, so nothing is granted role-wide or to any other user.

**UI:** `app/(dashboard)/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` — new "Cost Access" `Card`, rendered only when `isSuperAdminViewer`, placed between "Change account type" and "Account actions". Real HTML checkbox (`name="can_view_costs" value="true" defaultChecked={profile.can_view_costs}`) plus a "Save Cost Access" button — works with zero client JS, matching every other action on this page. Added `"cost-access-updated": "Cost access updated."` to the success-message map.

**Data Entry / non-Super-Admin exposure:** the card is gated by `isSuperAdminViewer` (in addition to the whole page already requiring `admin.users.manage`), so a non-Super-Admin who somehow reaches this page cannot see or submit the control; the server action independently re-checks `role.slug === "super_admin"` regardless of what the client sends, so the gate cannot be bypassed by posting the form directly. `costs.view` role permission and every other profile's `can_view_costs` are untouched — Data Entry accounts remain at `false` unless a Super Admin explicitly flips this control for that specific account.

**Files changed:** `app/actions/user-access.ts` (new `updateUserCostAccessAction`), `app/(dashboard)/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` (new Cost Access card + success message), `scripts/verify-admin-cost-access-toggle-unit10g4.mjs` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration, no schema change, no calculation change. `scripts/verify-admin-cost-access-toggle-unit10g4.mjs` (rolled-back transaction) confirms: `canViewCosts()` (the same canonical gate used everywhere) flips its answer purely off `profile.can_view_costs` for a Manager-equivalent context with no `costs.view` permission; the action's own DB write (grant → audit log → revoke) round-trips correctly against a real disposable profile row; `maintenance_data_entry`'s role permissions are untouched by this unit. No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.5 — Manager Dashboard Labor Cost Period Summary Fix

**Requirement:** the Manager dashboard only showed "Labor Hours Today"/"Labor Cost Today," which reads as broken when a worker's sessions were recorded yesterday or earlier (Today can legitimately be 0). Add This Week/This Month labor totals alongside Today, without touching schema, work-session calculation, `hourly_rate_snapshot` behavior, or Data Entry's cost visibility.

**Task 1 — confirmed, not a calculation bug:** `Labor Hours Today`/`Labor Cost Today` were already correctly scoped to `started_at >= todayStart` and already read `0`/`0.000 KWD` with no sessions today — verified by `scripts/verify-manager-labor-period-summary-unit10g5.mjs`'s empty-work-order case. The "looks broken" symptom was a display gap (no Week/Month figure to show the labor actually happened), not a data or calculation defect.

**New read — `getLaborPeriodTotals`** (`lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts`, new): a company-wide, visibility-scoped Today/This Week/This Month total. Deliberately NOT derived from the dashboard's existing `getWorkOrderLaborSummariesBulk` map, because that map (as called from this dashboard) only ever covers the ~30 most-recently-updated ACTIVE Job Cards — a Job Card worked on this week but already Closed would silently disappear from a week/month total built that way, reproducing the exact "not updating" confusion this unit exists to fix. One query (sessions with `started_at >= monthStart`, `status != Cancelled`, filtered through the `work_orders` relation by the caller's own visibility filter), bucketed in-memory into today/week/month — same "fetch once, bucket by boundary" convention `getWorkerActivityDetail` already established, same Sunday-start week boundary, same `duration_minutes`/`calculated_amount` fields (a corrected session's current stored values are summed automatically; cancelled sessions excluded by the query itself).

Three call sites' fallback default objects updated for the new required fields: `app/actions/closure-requests.ts`, `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` (closure requests modal), `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx`.

- Labor Snapshot card: header renamed `Labor Snapshot Today` → `Labor Snapshot` (it now covers all three periods); new compact period-summary block — `Today` / `This Week` / `This Month`, each `Xh` plus (only when `mgCanViewCosts`) `/ X.XXX KWD` — all three sourced from the same `mgLaborPeriodTotals`, so they can never disagree with each other or with the KPI row.
- Top Workers and Job Card Labor Cost now default to **This Week** (was Today/all-time respectively) per the task's own recommendation ("meaningful current workload") — `mgWorkerWeekTotals` (renamed from `mgWorkerTodayTotals`) and `mgJobCardLaborRows` both switched to the new `week_minutes`/`week_amount` fields; still scoped to the same active/recent 30-Job-Card sample as before (unchanged convention, matches Task 4's "active/recent Job Cards" wording).

**Task 6 — cost visibility:** unchanged mechanism — every new figure (period summary, Top Workers pay, Job Card Labor Cost pay) is gated by the same `mgCanViewCosts` (`canViewCostsForContext(context)`) already used everywhere else on this dashboard; Data Entry never reaches this Manager-only section of the page at all.

**Task 7 — realtime:** already fully satisfied before this unit — `REALTIME_EVENTS.JOB_CARD_WORK_STARTED/WORK_PAUSED/WORK_STOPPED/WORK_TIME_UPDATED` (`lib/realtime/events.ts`) are all `"job_card.*"` keys, already emitted from `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts`, and the dashboard's existing `<RealtimeRefresh watch={["job_card.", ...]}>` already matches all four by prefix. No realtime code change needed; confirmed by reading the emit sites and the watch list, not assumed.

No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.6 — Worker Profile Form Simplification and Division Rename

**Requirement:** simplify the Data Entry Add Worker form to a company-style 5-field flow (Employee ID, Name, Worker Type, Division, Hourly Rate), rename "Skill Category" to "Division" in the UI everywhere, remove Phone/Notes from creation, and update the Worker Profiles list/search/assignment picker accordingly — display-only + one additive migration, no work-session/rate-calculation change.

**Migration (Task 1):** `prisma/migrations/20260810000000_worker_profiles_employee_id_unit10g6` — additive nullable `employee_id text` column on `worker_profiles`, plus a partial unique index (`worker_profiles_employee_id_active_unique`) scoped to `employee_id IS NOT NULL AND is_active = true`, mirroring the existing name+phone active-only duplicate-check convention (`findDuplicateActiveWorker`) so a deactivated worker's Employee ID can be reused by a genuine replacement hire. Applied to the local dev DB via `npx prisma migrate deploy` (30th migration; `CLAUDE.md`'s Current Database State line updated). A dev server on port 3000 was holding a file lock on the Prisma query engine DLL, blocking `npx prisma generate` — stopped with explicit user confirmation, then the client regenerated cleanly; the user needs to run `npm run dev` again.

**Service layer (Task 1/7):** `lib/backend/workers/service.ts` — `WorkerProfileRow`/`toRow` carry `employee_id`; new `findDuplicateEmployeeId` (case-insensitive via the existing `normalizeMaterialKey`, active-only, `excludeId`-aware for edits) wired into both `createWorkerProfile` and `updateWorkerProfile` alongside the existing name+phone check, giving a clean error message before the DB's partial unique index would ever fire as a hard backstop. `listWorkerProfiles`'s search now also matches `employee_id`/`skill_category`. `lib/backend/workers/validators.ts` — `employeeId` added to `workerProfileSchema` (optional, trimmed, max 50 — schema-level optional so existing profiles without one can still be edited/saved, per Task 8). `app/actions/workers.ts` parses `employee_id` from the form.

**Division rename (Task 2):** UI label changed to "Division" in `components/admin/worker-profile-form-modal.tsx` (form field), `components/admin/worker-profiles-view.tsx` (list column header), `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/assignments/page.tsx` ("All Skill Categories" → "All Divisions" filter option). The underlying `skill_category` DB column, Prisma field, `SKILL_CATEGORIES` constant name, and every stored value are unchanged — confirmed via grep that no other file displays a literal "Skill Category" label (worker-card.tsx/worker-activity-detail-modal.tsx only render the raw value, no label text). `lib/backend/workers/constants.ts`'s `SKILL_CATEGORIES` gained `"Civil"` and `"General"` (the task's suggested value set) alongside the existing `Auto`/`Mechanical`/`Electrical`/`Other` — purely additive, no stored data affected.

**Add Worker modal (Task 1/3/4):** `components/admin/worker-profile-form-modal.tsx` reordered to Employee ID → Name → Worker Type → Division → Hourly Rate, matching the task's spec exactly. Employee ID is `required` only on create (`!worker`) — left optional on edit so an existing pre-Unit-10G.6 profile with no Employee ID yet isn't blocked from being saved for an unrelated change (Task 8). Phone/Notes fields now render only when `worker` is set (edit mode) — Option A, chosen because this modal already only ever opens in edit mode for Manager/Super Admin (Data Entry has no Edit button, enforced both by the caller hiding the button and server-side by `assertCanEditWorkerProfile`), so gating on `Boolean(worker)` alone correctly restricts Phone/Notes to Manager/Super Admin without a new prop. The Hourly Rate field/helper text ("Hourly rate is saved for Manager review and cannot be edited by Data Entry after creation.") were already exactly as Task 4 specifies from a prior unit (10F.4) — unchanged.

**Worker Profiles list (Task 5):** `components/admin/worker-profiles-view.tsx` — Employee ID column added (`w.employee_id ?? "—"`); Phone/Notes columns removed entirely for every role (the task's own Manager/Super-Admin "Show" list excludes Phone too — it's edit-only now, Option A); the whole Actions column (Edit/Deactivate) is omitted for Data Entry (`canManageWorkerProfiles` false) rather than rendered with a placeholder dash; search placeholder and matching logic updated to Employee ID/Name/Division (`useMemo` filter). `colSpan` on the empty-state row recomputed to match the now-conditional column count.

**Search / assignment picker (Task 6):** `components/work-orders/work-order-wizard.tsx`'s `WorkerPickerField` (the searchable "New Job Card" assignment picker) — `matchesWorkerQuery` now also matches `employee_id`; the dropdown result row prefixes the Employee ID before the name; placeholder text updated to "Search {label} by employee ID, name, or division…". The selected-worker chip already showed name only for every caller (verified, no role-conditional logic needed — Task 6's "name only" requirement was already satisfied). `InternalTeamRosterForm` (a separate, non-searchable `<select multiple>` picker used elsewhere) was left untouched — it has no search feature to extend, and Task 9's manual test steps specifically describe the wizard's searchable picker.

**Files changed:** `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260810000000_worker_profiles_employee_id_unit10g6/migration.sql` (new), `lib/backend/workers/constants.ts`, `lib/backend/workers/validators.ts`, `lib/backend/workers/service.ts`, `app/actions/workers.ts`, `components/admin/worker-profile-form-modal.tsx`, `components/admin/worker-profiles-view.tsx`, `components/work-orders/work-order-wizard.tsx`, `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/assignments/page.tsx`, `CLAUDE.md` (migration count), `scripts/verify-worker-profile-employee-id-unit10g6.mjs` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. `scripts/verify-worker-profile-employee-id-unit10g6.mjs` (rolled-back transactions): a worker with no Employee ID still saves/reads back safely as `null`; Employee ID stored as entered; the service-level duplicate check is case-insensitive and active-only (a deactivated worker's ID can be reused); the migration's own DB-level partial unique index blocks two ACTIVE workers sharing an Employee ID (and leaves nothing behind on failure) while allowing two INACTIVE workers to share one; `SKILL_CATEGORIES` includes Civil/General without losing any existing value. No work-session calculation, `hourly_rate_snapshot` behavior, or assignment logic touched — only field display/mapping and one additive column. No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.7 — Critical Workflow Popup Review Modal Instead of Direct Navigation

**Requirement:** the two Manager-facing critical popups (Closure Approval Needed, New Active Job Card) navigated straight to the full Job Card detail page on primary-button click, forcing the Manager off the dashboard. Clicking Review should open a review modal in place instead, with "Open Full Job Card" preserved as an explicit fallback — notification popup UX only, no workflow/approval/materials/session-calculation logic touched or duplicated.

**Payload/rule changes (Task 1/2/4/5):** `lib/notifications/critical-popup.ts` — `CriticalPopupPayload` gained `workOrderId`, `reviewMode` (`"closure_review" | "job_card_summary" | null`), and `jobCardDetailHref` (always the canonical `/maintenance/work-orders/{id}` URL, computed independently of `action_url`). `PopupRule` gained an optional `reviewMode`. The two Manager rules changed: `job_card.closure_requested` → `primaryLabel: "Review Closure"`, `reviewMode: "closure_review"`; `job_card.created`/`job_card.started` → `primaryLabel: "View Summary"`, `reviewMode: "job_card_summary"`. When a rule declares `reviewMode`, its `secondaryLabel`/`secondaryHref` are now always computed as `"Open Full Job Card"` / `jobCardDetailHref` (Task 5), overriding any rule-level static secondary. Every Data Entry rule (`job_card.closed`, `job_card.assignment_updated`) is completely untouched — `reviewMode` stays `undefined`/`null` for them, so their `primaryLabel`, plain-link behavior, and existing static secondary actions (e.g. "Open Daily Activity") are unchanged.

**Popup component (Task 1/3/6):** `components/notifications/critical-workflow-popup.tsx` — new `reviewing` state (`{ notificationId, workOrderId, mode }`) alongside the existing `popup` state. Primary-button click on a `reviewMode` popup now renders a `{ kind: "button", onClick: openReview }` action (via `WorkflowSuccessAction`'s existing `"button"` variant — no `WorkflowSuccessModal` change needed) that swaps the critical popup for `ClosureReviewModal` or `JobCardSummaryModal` in place, instead of the previous `{ kind: "link", href }` that navigated away. `activeIdRef` (the existing "only one popup at a time" guard) stays set through the whole reviewing session, so no second popup can appear underneath the review modal. Non-`reviewMode` popups (Data Entry's rules) keep the exact original `markReadAndClose` + Link behavior.

**Notification read timing (Task 6):** a new `onLoaded?: () => void` prop was added to `ClosureReviewModal` (`components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx`) — called exactly once, guarded by a `hasCalledOnLoaded` ref, the first time its detail fetch succeeds; existing callers (the Closure Requests dashboard section) simply don't pass it, so their behavior is unchanged. `JobCardSummaryModal` (new) takes the same `onLoaded` prop with the same one-shot-on-success contract. `critical-workflow-popup.tsx`'s `markReviewLoaded()` (passed as `onLoaded`) is what actually calls `markNotificationReadAction` — so the notification is marked read only once the review modal's data has genuinely loaded, never on click alone, and never if the fetch fails (the `loadError` branch in either modal never calls `onLoaded`). Closing a review modal that never successfully loaded re-adds its notification id to the existing session-scoped dismissed-ids list (same mechanism the original Dismiss button already used) so it isn't silently lost; closing one that DID load is a no-op beyond resetting local state, since it's already been marked read.

**Approval flow (Task 3):** `approveAndCloseReview()` (passed as `ClosureReviewModal`'s `onApproved`) closes the review modal and calls `router.refresh()`, refreshing the dashboard's KPI/closure-requests count — mirrors the exact pattern already used by `ClosureRequestsModal`'s own `onApproved` handler. The "Job Card Closed" success toast is already dispatched inside `ClosureReviewModal` itself (from a prior unit) — not duplicated. `approveJobCardClosureModalAction` (the existing closure-approval server action) is unchanged and reused as-is — no approval logic duplicated anywhere in this unit.

**New Active Job Card summary (Task 4/7):** `app/actions/job-card-summary.ts` (new) — `getJobCardSummaryAction`, a deliberately lightweight, Manager/Super-Admin-only (`assertIsManagerRole`, mirroring `closure-requests.ts`'s own helper), visibility-scoped read: one `work_orders.findFirst` (asset, issue, status, created_at, `worker_type` as "work team", `_count` for attachments — never the full attachment rows), one active-assignment count, one `findFirst` for any Active/Paused session (not a full session-history fetch), and the existing lightweight `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrder`. Derives `assignmentStatusLabel` (mirrors the dashboard's own "N workers · Working Now/Paused" wording), `materialsStatusLabel`, and a simple deterministic `nextAction` (materials shortage > no workers assigned > active session > "review and confirm"). `components/dashboard/job-card-summary-modal.tsx` (new) renders this via the same `LargeFormModal` shell `ClosureReviewModal` uses, with exactly the task's three actions — Open Daily Activity, Open Full Job Card, Dismiss — and deliberately no approval action (starting a Job Card needs no Manager approval).

**Realtime (Task 8):** unchanged — `critical-workflow-popup.tsx` still uses the one shared `useRealtimeConnection().subscribe("notification", ...)` call; no new `EventSource`. The relevant events (`job_card.closure_requested/started/created/closed/work_time_updated`, `material_ledger.*`, `offline_inventory.*`) were already emitted and already drive the dashboard's existing `RealtimeRefresh` — neither the emission sites nor the dashboard's watch list were touched.

**Role/cost visibility (Task 9):** unchanged by construction — `rulesForRole()` only returns `MANAGER_RULES` for `context.role?.slug === "maintenance_manager"`; Data Entry always resolves `DATA_ENTRY_RULES` (no `reviewMode` anywhere in that table), so Data Entry can never trigger the new review-modal path client-side. Both `getClosureReviewDetailAction` and the new `getJobCardSummaryAction` independently re-check `assertIsManagerRole` server-side regardless of what the client requests — defense in depth, same pattern as every other Manager-only action in this codebase. `canViewCosts` gating inside `ClosureReviewModal` is untouched.

**Files changed:** `lib/notifications/critical-popup.ts`, `components/notifications/critical-workflow-popup.tsx`, `components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx` (new optional `onLoaded` prop only), `app/actions/job-card-summary.ts` (new), `components/dashboard/job-card-summary-modal.tsx` (new), `scripts/verify-critical-popup-review-modal-unit10g7.mjs` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. `scripts/verify-critical-popup-review-modal-unit10g7.mjs` (rolled-back transaction + pure-logic mirrors): confirms the two changed rules' exact primary labels/`reviewMode`/`workOrderId`/`jobCardDetailHref`/"Open Full Job Card" secondary; confirms Data Entry's rules are byte-for-byte unaffected; confirms the summary action's assignment-status/materials-status/next-action derivation against real rows (no workers → "Assign workers", active session → "Monitor progress in Daily Activity", materials shortage takes priority); confirms attachments are counted via `_count`, never fetched in full. No schema change, no approval/closure/materials/worker-session-calculation logic changed or duplicated. No deployment performed.
